chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:

From the good fortune of a person is that his business is in his own city, and his companions are righteous, and he has children whom he can seek assistance from; and from the misery of a person is that he has a wife with whom he is fascinated, yet she betrays him.

key_terms.مَتْجَر: Business, trade, or place of commerce

ai.seo_question: What are the key indicators of a person's happiness and misery according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) to highlight the Shia emphasis on social stability and familial integrity as markers of divine favor. The narration contrasts the peace of mind derived from local economic security and righteous companionship with the spiritual distress caused by marital infidelity, reflecting the practical ethics of daily life in early Shia communities. This teaching underscores the interplay between material circumstances and moral character in achieving true sa'adah (happiness).
